raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not like taking big risks. What I know is what I saw on my own land and what the people around me do. Wheat and maize are still my steady crops, because even if the price is not great, they feed the family and usually give cash every year. Cotton can bring money too, but it needs more watching and more picking, so I will not put too much land into it. Some people in my house work outside, so labor is not always in hand. Because of that, I will keep things close to what worked before, use the well when the crop really needs water, and not push fertilizer too high because every extra bag costs money.

For the wheat-maize land, I will keep most of it in the usual rotation, because changing now is troublesome and risky. I will put fertilizer in round amounts, a bit heavy rather than too light, because if the crop turns yellow later it is hard to fix. For cotton, I will keep a smaller piece. Cotton can make money, but it needs more labor over a long time, and at my age I cannot chase it too hard. So this year I will farm steadily, spend carefully, and aim for a harvest that is safe more than fancy.
